title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named Uptown and Dickinson Avenue destinations in Greenville, the downtown area directly beside ECU’s main campus.

cards.title: Greenville Town Common
cards.subtitle: East 1st Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Walk the paved riverwalk and green space at this 21-acre Town Common, then check the venue calendar if you want to pair the stop with a public event.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront public-green-space stop beside Uptown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town Common has 21 acres of open green space, paved connections to the South Tar River Greenway, and a 1,500-foot riverwalk.
cards.source_title: Greenville Town Common | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: Located at 105 East 1st Street; event programming varies.

cards.title: Greenville Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: South Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Use the museum’s exhibit schedule to choose a visit, and allow time to look through both the permanent collection and any traveling exhibition on view.
cards.short_summary: A named Evans Street museum with permanent and traveling art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville Museum of Art presents 19th- and 20th-century American art from its permanent collection alongside traveling exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Greenville Museum of Art | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 802 South Evans Street; classes, workshops, and events may have separate requirements.

cards.title: Emerge Gallery and Art Center
cards.subtitle: South Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Check the rotating gallery program before you go, or look for an age-appropriate class or workshop offered by the Pitt County Arts Council.
cards.short_summary: A downtown arts center with two changing galleries and creative programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerge is home to the Pitt County Arts Council and has two galleries with rotating exhibits, a sales gallery, and classes and workshops.
cards.source_title: Emerge Gallery and Art Center | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 404 South Evans Street; workshop enrollment and exhibition access may vary.

cards.title: The Scullery Coffee House & Creamery
cards.subtitle: Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Use this named Evans Street coffee-and-creamery stop as a daytime anchor while walking between Uptown destinations; confirm menu and seating directly before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A coffee house and creamery on the central Uptown corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Scullery Coffee House & Creamery is located at 431 Evans Street in Greenville.
cards.source_title: The Scullery Coffee House & Creamery | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 431 Evans Street; purchases are required for food or drinks.

cards.title: Emerald City Collective
cards.subtitle: East 4th Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Look for current pop-up or gallery details before heading over, especially during the First Friday ArtWalk season when the space hosts participating artists.
cards.short_summary: A downtown gallery and pop-up shop that participates in First Friday ArtWalk.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerald City Collective is a gallery and pop-up shop at 106 East 4th Street and participates in Downtown Greenville First Friday ArtWalks from September through June.
cards.source_title: Emerald City Collective | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 106 East 4th Street; pop-up and ArtWalk participation are seasonal or event-specific.

cards.title: Greenville-Pitt County Visitors Center
cards.subtitle: Cotanche Street corridor, Downtown Greenville
cards.notes: Start here to pick up local orientation help, then use the nearby garage or surface lots if you are arriving by car for an Uptown walk.
cards.short_summary: A Cotanche Street visitor-information stop across from the Fourth Street garage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville-Pitt County Convention & Visitors Bureau operates its Visitors Center at 417 Cotanche Street, Suite 100, across from the Fourth Street Parking Garage.
cards.access_notes: 417 Cotanche Street, Suite 100; the visitor center lists Monday–Friday daytime service.

cards.title: The Martinsborough
cards.subtitle: South Evans Street corridor, Uptown Greenville
cards.notes: Pause outside to photograph the restored Jefferson Blount-Harvey Building, then consult the venue’s calendar if you are considering an event-based visit.
cards.short_summary: A restored 1923 building used as a downtown special-events venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Martinsborough occupies the restored Jefferson Blount-Harvey Building, built in 1923, and serves as a venue for special events and receptions.
cards.access_notes: 330 South Evans Street; access depends on private or scheduled events.

cards.title: Dickinson Avenue Farmers & Makers Market
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Avenue corridor, Dickinson Avenue District
cards.notes: Browse the indoor market’s seasonal vendor mix in the former bottling plant, and check current vendors or hours before making the walk from campus.
cards.short_summary: An indoor, year-round market in a former Cher-Cola bottling plant.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dickinson Avenue Farmers & Makers Market is an indoor, year-round market in a 100-year-old former Cher-Cola bottling plant featuring items made or grown within 50 miles of Greenville.
cards.source_title: Dickinson Avenue Farmers & Makers Market | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 716 Dickinson Avenue; purchases are optional and vendor offerings vary.

cards.title: The Greenville Metal Zoo
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Avenue corridor at 9th Street
cards.notes: Walk the Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street area to view the repurposed-metal sculptures, then keep an eye out for additional works around Downtown businesses.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sculpture stop centered at Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Greenville Metal Zoo is an outdoor sculpture park of repurposed-metal works by artist Jonathan Bowling, centered at Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street.
cards.source_title: The Greenville Metal Zoo | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works are described at the Dickinson Avenue and 9th Street intersection and elsewhere downtown.

cards.title: Native Fine Diner
cards.subtitle: Dickinson Avenue corridor, Dickinson Avenue Historic District
cards.notes: Use the former Carolina Grill Diner building as a documented Dickinson Avenue landmark, and check the restaurant directly for current service details before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A restored former diner building in the Dickinson Avenue Historic District.
cards.evidence_claim: Native Fine Diner is at 907 Dickinson Avenue in the restored location of Greenville’s former Carolina Grill Diner, within the Historic Dickinson Avenue Arts District.
cards.source_title: Native Fine Diner | Visit Greenville-Pitt County
cards.access_notes: 907 Dickinson Avenue; purchases are required for restaurant offerings.
